subject: Update: EdgeBridge proxy added as transient subprocessor — routing impact for EU customers
messages:
From: EdgeBridge Compliance <compliance@edgebridge.io>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: transient proxy (EdgeBridge) added to subprocessor roster

Hi David,

Quick heads-up: EdgeBridge will be added as a transient subprocessor in our delivery pipeline starting next week for a short pilot period. The change affects how certain telemetric routing and TLS termination are handled for low-latency EU edge requests.

What this means for Redwood customers (brief):
- A small fraction (~2-4%) of requests originating from EU regions may be routed through EdgeBridge proxy points for connection warm-up and edge caching.
- No customer data is persisted by EdgeBridge beyond short-lived TLS session state and transient logs (retention: 48 hours).
- We will not perform any model inference or store PII.

Attachments: edgebridge-dpa-addendum.pdf (pdf, 342KB), edge-proxy-flow-diagram.png (png, 78KB)

We wanted to notify your team and surface any exportability / SCC / DPA issues early. If you need specific evidence (SOC2 control coverage, encryption attestations, or log retention snapshots) we can provide those artifacts by Friday.

Regards,
Leila Moreno
Head of Compliance, EdgeBridge
compliance@edgebridge.io

--
EdgeBridge | fast-edge proxying for real-time apps
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Leila Moreno <leila@edgebridge.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: transient proxy (EdgeBridge) added as a subprocessor — routing impact for EU customers

Leila,

Thanks for the heads-up — appreciate the proactive notice. A few follow-ups from our side to evaluate risk for AuroraPay and other EU customers:

1) Can you confirm the exact egress countries for the proxy points used in the pilot? We need a country-level list to validate export restrictions.
2) Please confirm that kv/prefix caches never include raw request payloads or customer content; we need a statement on what is cached and for how long.
3) SOC2 scope: can you provide the specific control IDs that cover transient logging and access controls, and a point contact for a short evidence pull if required?
4) Will EdgeBridge sign our standard DPA addendum or do we need to execute your addendum? Attached is a quick worksheet (subprocessor-impact-matrix.xlsx) that we use to triage new processors — please fill out if possible.

Action: Kimberly, can you review the attachments and flag anything blocking for AuroraPay? Marissa, loop in procurement/legal if you see contract work needed.

Best,
David
David Kim
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: EdgeBridge Compliance <compliance@edgebridge.io>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: transient proxy (EdgeBridge) added as a subprocessor — routing impact for EU customers

David / team,

Thanks — answers inline and attached. Summary:

- Egress countries: Ireland (IE), Netherlands (NL), Germany (DE) for this pilot. We will not route through the U.S. for EU-originating sessions.
- Cache policy: only TLS session identifiers and ephemeral connection metadata are buffered. No request bodies, no customer payloads, and no KV caches containing customer content. Retention: 48 hours, automatic purge.
- SOC2 coverage: SOC2 Type II (CC-1x, CC-3x) covers transient logging and access controls for the proxy fleet. See attached evidence slice: "SOC2-proxy-excerpt.pdf" (included in edgebridge-dpa-addendum.pdf).
- DPA: We are happy to sign Redwood's DPA addendum. We attached our proposed addendum language as a tracked-change PDF inside edgebridge-dpa-addendum.pdf; we're open to your preferred workflow (redlines via DocuSign or return a signed copy).

Attached: edgebridge-dpa-addendum.pdf, edge-proxy-flow-diagram.png

If you want a short call, Leila and our engineering lead can join tomorrow morning UTC.

Regards,
Leila Moreno
Head of Compliance, EdgeBridge
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Leila Moreno <leila@edgebridge.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: transient proxy (EdgeBridge) added as a subprocessor — routing impact for EU customers

Leila — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. I reviewed the addendum and the diagram; a few internal notes and next steps:

- Kimberly: please confirm if the Ireland/Netherlands/Germany routing footprint is acceptable for AuroraPay (region: eu). If there are any additional residency constraints, call them out here by EOD.
- Marissa / Procurement: EdgeBridge indicated willingness to sign our addendum; can your team take the attached PDF and prepare a redline workflow? If DocuSign is preferred by EdgeBridge, let's prepare the DocuSign envelope and include the SOC2 excerpt.
- Legal/Privacy: Jordan, can you review the retention language (48 hours) and the cache statement and confirm whether an exception memo is required for customers that have stricter retention?

I'll tentatively approve the pilot for EU low-latency routing contingent on: (a) Kimberly's OK on residency, (b) legal sign-off on retention cache wording, and (c) EdgeBridge executes our DPA addendum or acceptable redline.

Action items (owners):
- EdgeBridge: execute DPA or accept Redwood redline (owner: EdgeBridge compliance) — due: 2029-03-18
- Kimberly: residency confirmation for AuroraPay — due: 2029-03-15 EOD
- Jordan/Legal: retention/caching sign-off or exception memo — due: 2029-03-17
- Marissa/Procurement: prepare DocuSign and contract steps — due: 2029-03-18

Thanks everyone — loop in anyone else if needed.

David
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
